blocks.text: Dohra:
There existed a hospice in the west, In the vicinity of Darbar Sahib was it located. There used to sit S. Sham Singh in this hospice. Of Buddha Dal Singhs was he a commander. (1)
lines: There existed a hospice in the west,
In the vicinity of Darbar Sahib was it located.
There used to sit S.
Sham Singh in this hospice.
Of Buddha Dal Singhs was he a commander.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
A chief of all Singh chiefs was he, Batchmate was he of S. Kapoor Singh. Buddha Dal had he commanded before S. Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, To Sandhu Jats and Narla village did he belong. (2)
lines: A chief of all Singh chiefs was he,
Batchmate was he of S.
Kapoor Singh.
Buddha Dal had he commanded before S.
Jassa Singh Ahluwalia,
To Sandhu Jats and Narla village did he belong.

blocks.text: First of all, a fort at Kathania did he raise, Defiance did he hurl at the Lahore rulers. Against Ahmed Shah Abdali did he wage a war, Into a wedlock did he enter after Abdali's departure. (3)
lines: First of all, a fort at Kathania did he raise,
Defiance did he hurl at the Lahore rulers.
Against Ahmed Shah Abdali did he wage a war,
Into a wedlock did he enter after Abdali's departure.

blocks.text: Whomsoever he gave a village or a fort as reward, Never did he ask him to return that award. Till today are his subordinates occupying those places. Sovereign owners did their descendents become of those properties. (4)
lines: Whomsoever he gave a village or a fort as reward,
Never did he ask him to return that award.
Till today are his subordinates occupying those places.
Sovereign owners did their descendents become of those properties.

blocks.text: Ten villages' territorial rights did he bestow on his daughter, Some of these villages were around Mirankot, others across the Satluj. Three hospices did he own at Amritsar, Himself he occupied the Central, alloting the side ones to his chiefs. (5)
lines: Ten villages' territorial rights did he bestow on his daughter,
Some of these villages were around Mirankot, others across the Satluj.
Three hospices did he own at Amritsar,
Himself he occupied the Central, alloting the side ones to his chiefs.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The hospice on the left side of Akal Takht, To Bihara Singh Sandhu from Chiddniwal was allotted. The hospice on the right side of Akal Takht, To S. Baghel Singh Dhaliwal from Jhabal was given. (6)
lines: The hospice on the left side of Akal Takht,
To Bihara Singh Sandhu from Chiddniwal was allotted.
The hospice on the right side of Akal Takht,
To S.
Baghel Singh Dhaliwal from Jhabal was given.

blocks.text: Dohra:
That hospice, being dilapidated, fell down, Which once belonged to S. Sham Singh. There at that site was "Gur Panth Prakash", composed, There were its two copies prepared and revised. (7)
lines: That hospice, being dilapidated, fell down,
Which once belonged to S.
Sham Singh.
There at that site was "Gur Panth Prakash", composed,
There were its two copies prepared and revised.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Whosoever reads and listens to its contents, In (Sikh) faith would he become determined. The way the author heard these episodes from his elders, So has he recorded those episodes in this volume. (8)
lines: Whosoever reads and listens to its contents,
In (Sikh) faith would he become determined.
The way the author heard these episodes from his elders,
So has he recorded those episodes in this volume.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Whosoever goes through those episodes, Whosoever listens again to its contents. Worthy of revered Guru's grace would he become, With faith in Sikhism would he be endowed. (9)
lines: Whosoever goes through those episodes,
Whosoever listens again to its contents.
Worthy of revered Guru's grace would he become,
With faith in Sikhism would he be endowed.

blocks.text: Swaiyya:

Thus has "Gur Panth Prakash" epic been completed, The way the Khalsa Panth evolved the same has he narrated. Whosoever participates in war after going through its contents, Never would such an enlightened Singh desert the field. Finally when such a warrior breathes his last, Instantly would his soul join the martyrs' fraternity. Among the martyrs would he join as spontaneously, As a drop of water mixes with the ocean water. (10)
lines: Thus has "Gur Panth Prakash" epic been completed,
The way the Khalsa Panth evolved the same has he narrated.
Whosoever participates in war after going through its contents,
Never would such an enlightened Singh desert the field.
Finally when such a warrior breathes his last,
Instantly would his soul join the martyrs' fraternity.
Among the martyrs would he join as spontaneously,
As a drop of water mixes with the ocean water.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whosoever reads and recites this epic with faith and devotion, With fulfillment of his cherished desires would he be rewarded. More profound shall be become in his faith in the Sikh Gurus, Even as all his wants and sufferings shall stand wiped out. (11)
lines: Whosoever reads and recites this epic with faith and devotion,
With fulfillment of his cherished desires would he be rewarded.
More profound shall be become in his faith in the Sikh Gurus,
Even as all his wants and sufferings shall stand wiped out.

blocks.text: Dohra:

At the holy shrine of Guru Ramdas, Darbar Sahib, With faith, devotion and means has the author worked. A devout service has Rattan Singh rendered unto the Guru, May God's blessings be upon His humble devotee. (12)
lines: At the holy shrine of Guru Ramdas,
Darbar Sahib,
With faith, devotion and means has the author worked.
A devout service has Rattan Singh rendered unto the Guru,
May God's blessings be upon His humble devotee.

blocks.text: Dohra:

It was in the year eighteen hundred and ninety eight1 , After having spent so many years on this epic. May the devout readers and listeners of this epic, Stay enriched, rewarded and blessed indeed. (13)
lines: It was in the year eighteen hundred and ninety eight1 ,
After having spent so many years on this epic.
May the devout readers and listeners of this epic,
Stay enriched, rewarded and blessed indeed.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Of S. Sham Singh is he (the author) the maternal grandson, Rattan Singh is the name of the author, In the vicinity of the sacred pool of Guru's shrine, Is he a resident of village Mirankot. (14)
lines: Of S.
Sham Singh is he (the author) the maternal grandson,
Rattan Singh is the name of the author,
In the vicinity of the sacred pool of Guru's shrine,
Is he a resident of village Mirankot.
